facts.statement: The genus Phosphorosaurus was first described by Louis Dollo in 1889.
facts.quote: authority: Dollo, 1889

facts.statement: Phosphorosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous, Maastrichtian

facts.statement: Phosphorosaurus belongs to the Halisaurinae subfamily of mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Phosphorosaurus is classified within the Halisaurinae subfamily alongside the genera Pluridens, Eonatator, and Halisaurus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Phosphorosaurus are found exclusively in Maastrichtian strata.
facts.quote: Stratigraphically, Phosphorosaurus is only known from the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Two species of Phosphorosaurus are known: P. ortliebi from Belgium and P. ponpetelegans from Japan.
facts.quote: Two species are known: Phosphorosaurus ortliebi, from the Craie de Ciply Formation in Belgium, and P. ponpetelegans, from the Hakobuchi Formation of Hokkaido in Japan.

facts.statement: P. ponpetelegans lived only in the earliest Maastrichtian, while P. ortliebi lived throughout the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: P. ponpetelegans is only known from the very earliest Maastrichtian, whilst P. ortliebi lived throughout the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Phosphorosaurus was an extinct marine lizard belonging to the mosasaur family.
facts.quote: Phosphorosaurus ("phosphate lizard") is an extinct genus of marine lizard belonging to the mosasaur family.

facts.statement: Analysis suggests Phosphorosaurus was a deep-water or nocturnal hunter that likely preyed on squid and bioluminescent fish.
facts.quote: Analysis of Phosphorosaurus biology suggests that this mosasaur was a deep-water or nocturnal hunter, potentially preying on animals such as squid and bioluminescent fish similar to the modern lanternfish present in the same areas.

facts.statement: Phosphorosaurus had large eyes with overlapping fields of vision that provided depth perception for hunting in low light.
facts.quote: The large eyes of Phosphorosaurus had overlapping fields of vision, giving it depth perception, which would have given it an advantage when chasing such animals in poorly-lit conditions.

facts.statement: Louis Dollo defined the genus in 1889 based on fossils from the upper Maastrichtian Craie phosphateé of Ciply in Belgium.
facts.quote: Belgian palaeontologist Louis Dollo defined the genus in 1889, with the description of Phosphorosaurus ortliebi from the upper Maastrichtian Craie phosphateé of Ciply in Belgium.

facts.statement: The holotype of Phosphorosaurus is a fragmented skull estimated to be around 42 cm long.
facts.quote: The holotype is a fragmented and incomplete skull that is estimated to have been around 42 cm long.

facts.statement: The species was reclassified as Halisaurus ortliebi in 1996, but later authorities rejected this due to cranial differences.
facts.quote: It was reclassified as Halisaurus ortliebi in 1996, but this was not taken up by later authorities due to differences in the cranium.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Phosphorosaurus ponpetelegans might represent a distinct genus that needs a new name rather than being part of Halisaurus.
facts.quote: They tentatively assigned these species to Halisaurus, with "Phosphorosaurus" ponpetelegans possibly representing a distinct genus in need of a new name.

facts.statement: The name P. ponpetelegans honors the clean Pankerusano-sawa Creek in Hokkaido where the exceptionally preserved holotype was found.
facts.quote: The etymology of P. ponpetelegans derives from the words "ponpet", which means "creek" in Ainu (language of the indigenous peoples of Hokkaido), and "elegans", Latin for "elegant", referencing the exceptional preservation of the holotype specimen of the species and the clean Pankerusano-sawa Creek where the fossil was discovered.

facts.statement: The two species of Phosphorosaurus can be distinguished by several specific fossil characters.
facts.quote: P. ortliebi and P. ponpetelgans can be distinguished from each other by several fossil characters.

facts.statement: Phosphorosaurus was a relatively small animal, measuring 3 to 4 meters in length compared to many other mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Con una longitud de 3–4 metros, era un animal relativamente pequeño comparado con muchos otros mosasáuridos.

facts.statement: Although often treated as a synonym of Halisaurus, a 2015 study recognizes Phosphorosaurus as a valid genus.
facts.quote: Aunque fue usualmente tratado como un sinónimo de Halisaurus, un estudio publicado en 2015 lo reconoce como un género válido.

facts.statement: Phosphorosaurus was an extinct mosasaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian).
facts.quote: Phosphorosaurus («lagarto de fósforo») es un género extinto de mosasáurido que vivió durante el Cretácico Superior (Maastrichtiense).

facts.statement: The parent group of Phosphorosaurus is Halisaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Halisaurini

facts.statement: Phosphorosaurus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: Phosphorosaurus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
